question.text: For a Cat III AIF investment made in a currency OTHER than INR, NAV determination requires:

answer.text: Conversion to INR at closing market rate on the relevant Valuation Day
Conversion at RBI reference rate of prior month

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the chapter: 'Determination of NAV should be done in Indian Rupee (INR). Any investment made in a currency, otherwise than in INR shall be converted into INR at closing market rate, on the relevant Valuation Day.' The Trap: The historical purchase rate freezes FX gains and losses incorrectly; a 6-month forward rate and a prior-month RBI reference rate are not the current closing spot rate on the Valuation Day. Note: The rule fixes both the currency (INR) and the rate (closing market rate on the Valuation Day) used for converting non-INR investments into NAV.
